newsitem.title: TAIWAN: "Dual" surge pushes Taiwan stocks to 7-year high.
newsitem.headline: "Dual" surge pushes Taiwan stocks to 7-year high.

text.p: A strong and rare confluence of Taiwan's bulwark financial and electronic sectors sent the stock index surging to another seven-year high close on Friday and brokers said they expected more rises ahead.
The index surged to a seven-year intraday high 8,895.34 and ended at 8,882.13, a gain of 245.84 points or 2.85 percent.
The surpassed Wednesday's seven-year closing high of 8,713.49. The index has not closed higher since ending at 8,922.67 on May 9, 1990.
Turnover was extremely heavy at T$213.6 billion, but still well below Thursday's all-time-high T$251 billion.
Financials surged 5.14 percent and electronics 2.42 percent -- a rare confluence of the heavily weighted and typically contrarian sectors that brokers dubbed "dual mainstreaming".
"The two most heavily weighted sectors are rising at the same time, indicating that a big bullish trend has emerged," said HSBC James Capel research manager Alex Chen.
Financials account for some 20 percent of the market's weighting, while electronics represent 12 percent, Chen said.
"The financials' surge was especially important as it's a signal the government wants the market to be bullish," he said, citing apparent state intervention through government funds.
Ruling party-linked China Development led the financial surge, rising the daily seven percent limit to T$140.
Top insurance firms Cathay Life and Shin Kong Life were limit up to T$163 and T$107, respectively.

The index opened 1.65 percent higher after chipmaker United Microelectronics on Thursday announced an ambitious T$500 billion, 10-year wafer fabrication project, Taiwan's single biggest investment scheme to date.
Electronics rebounded 2.42 percent from Thursday's 4.01 percent plunge, with United Microelectronics limit up to T$103.
